- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to under-forecast sharp upward moves; adjust upward by 2–5% for early positive sentiment.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast is rising, model often over-optimistic; reduce forecast by 3–7% if recent sentiment is negative or neutral.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use mean-reversion to 10–15 day average.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model tends to hold high forecast; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of deviation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility in early period; apply downward bias of 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows a recent 0.50 (moderate bullish) followed by 0.00, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–4% after 0.50 sentiment to avoid overcorrection.
